#1411. Cesc Fabregas's Como win NINE-ONE in the biggest away victory in Champions League history - two weeks after thrashing Michael Carrick's Man United - in just their first year at Europe's top table

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and LUKE POWER, SPORTS REPORTER

Published: 17:01 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 17:59 EST, 8 November 2026

Manchester United's 4-1 battering by Como two weeks ago now looks a lucky escape – after the Italian side romped to a 9-1 victory at Lens in the Champions League.

Cesc Fabregas' side put in a stunning performance in a record-equalling win which well and truly announced them as contenders on the biggest stage.

Como now sit fourth in the Champions League standings after also thrashing RB Leipzig and Man United, who are likely relieved that Lens took such a pounding.

It means only Paris Saint-Germain, Real Madrid, and Arsenal have got off to better starts, despite this being their maiden season in European competition.

The lakeside outfit were 3-0 up at half-time – with the scorer of the third goal, Nico Paz, paying his respects to late Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel – before a rout after the break.

It is the latest statement win for Como, whose transformation began in 2019 when a pair of Indonesian billionaire brothers, who originally made their fortune in the tobacco industry, bought the club for $850,000 (£644,427) through their Djarum Group.

Como thrashed Lens 9-1 in a record-equalling victory in the Champions League on Wednesday

Cesc Fabregas is quickly building his name as one of the most talented coaches in Europe

With a combined net worth then estimated at $48billion (£36.4billion), Robert Budi Hartono and Michael Bambang Hartono instantly made Como the richest club in Italian football.

Rather than pursue instant success through lavish spending, Como have built steadily, investing in infrastructure, recruitment, and a clear footballing identity – and it is paying off big-time.

They have now won six games on the bounce, though they still sit fourth in Serie A five points behind leaders Lazio, who have had an almost perfect start.

Their crushing of Lens was the first time an Italian side had scored seven or more goals away from home in European Cup/Champions League history.

And their hat-trick hero on the night, Anastasios Douvikas, is now the top scorer in the Champions League ahead of Erling Haaland.

All of this comes for a side who were playing in the third tier just six seasons ago and on the back of a relatively modest summer spend of £58million on nine permanent arrivals and loanees.

'Today everything went our way,' said an ecstatic Fabregas post-match. 'A great night for Como and our fans.'

There was a poignant moment when Paz paid homage to Miguel and his hometown club, holding aloft a shirt with the picture of the late star alongside the caption: 'Rest in peace.' Though he plays for Argentina, Paz was born in Tenerife and also spent time in the club's youth system from 2014-16.

Miguel died on Tuesday morning less than 24 hours after a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during their Spanish second division match on Monday. Having suffered serious head and chest injuries he subsequently suffered a cardiac arrest.

Como's Nico Paz paid tribute to Jesus de Miguel during his goalscoring celebration vs Lens

Despite playing for Argentina, Paz was born in Tenerife and also played for their youth teams

Tenerife striker De Miguel died on Tuesday morning after a horrifying clash with Jesus Owono

Como led 3-0 at half-time with hat-trick hero Douvikas scoring two at that point before Paz's goal and his De Miguel tribute.

Soon after the interval the Serie A outfit crushed any notion of the hosts coming back as they plundered in five goals in a devastating 22-minute spell which included Douvikas completing his hat-trick. Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martina Baturina also got in on the act during that period.

Ruben Aguilar pulled one back for Lens before Matteo Papaccioli rounded off the rout in stoppage time. The 18-year-old Papaccioli, who came on in the second half, is a member of Como's youth team and hasn't even played in Serie A yet.

Wednesday's win means Como have broken many records in the Champions League.

The Italian side matched the eight-goal winning margins recorded by Liverpool and Real Madrid in their 8-0 home victories over Besiktas and Malmo respectively. They also became only the second team after Bayern Munich to score nine goals in a Champions League match.

Como followed their 4-1 victory over Manchester United with another emphatic performance, becoming the first team to score nine goals away from home in the European Cup since 1971 – Feyenoord beat Olympiacos Nicosia by this scoreline – as they climbed to fourth in the standings on nine points. The previous best scoring performance by an away club in the Champions League was Bayern Munich's 8-2 win over Barcelona at a neutral venue (Lisbon) in 2020.

Fabregas's side may have made Champions League record-equalling history, but Feyenoord hold the European Cup mark for most goals scored in a single match, having beaten Icelandic side KR 12-2 in September 1969.

Lens, who suffered the heaviest defeat by a French club in the competition, are 33rd with three points.

Justin heads the ball to Ampadu who plays a one-two with Stach then chips the ball 40 yards, a real up and under, for Calvert-Lewin to chase. Raya beats him to it.

Aresnal launch a counter up the right and the telepathy between White and Saka for once breaks down when White runs offside for a return pass. Elvedi was there to sweep up in any case.

Muharemovic reads the game well and snuffs out a long pass looking for Havertz, shifts the ball up to Calvert-Lewin who is grabbed round the waist by Gabriel and Leeds are awarded a free-kick in the centre-circle.

Saka, miles offside, takes on a cross that he should have headed with a leaping volley instead and Trafford saves at very close range. Slick work between Odegaard and Madueke to get the ball to Saka.

Both sides used the opportunity of the playing of The Angel to muster in huddles. Leeds kick off, attacking from right to left, going all the way back to Trafford standing outside his box and he clips a long pass up the right and Leeds are immediately penalised with the linesman’s flag.

Arsenal switch to their right and try to free Saka but Trafford comes out to kick it into touch.

Arsenal in red and white, Leeds in yellow and black. Ben White was looking round to see if there was anyone in the Leeds line he recognised from his excellent year’s loan with them but Marcelo Bielsa’s promotion heroes have all moved on now. In fact, with Illan Meslier, there are two at the Gunners and none at Elland Road.

Long international break, we recovered most of our players and have a point to prove after our last game.

[Declan Rice] needed that [break] after everything he’s done over the years. He has looked fresh this week.

Everyone is fit and ready to play but we have a very difficult opponent.

We know that today is one of the toughest tasks in European football. They have been the most consistent side in Europe for years. Especially after a warning shot in the last game, they will be on it today.

But we didn’t win our good start in the lottery we earned it. We travel here in confidence.

Brighton didn’t park the bus. They went for it and pressed Arsenal. You need to do this. You have to go for it. If you sit deep their individual quality is too good. The one thing is to have a plan and a theory but another to execute it.

Last season we faced one of the best sides in the world so we didn’t dwell on [those defeats]. If we are at our best we have a chance to compete for points.

There’s no doubt who the biggest threat to Arsenal’s defence will be today: Dominic Calvert-Lewin has four goals in six games in all competitions this season and is the top scoring Englishman in the league since the start of last season. He’s a player Arsenal once looked at signing, many years ago.

Joe Cole is trying to make a case that Manchester City are not guilty of cheating because financial doping is not the same as taking drugs or match-fixing. A man who won all his medals at Abramovich’s Chelsea says it ‘is not right to class it as cheating’.

This is where punditry is broken. A former player may have an opinion on the subject of finance but it does not sound as though he is particularly informed and yet he’s given time to witter on because he doesn’t ‘feel’ it’s right.

The most interesting aspect of that Arsenal lineup, I think, is the inclusion of Noni Madueke. It seems like he’ll be on the left flank, as the replacement for the injured Christos Tzolis. Madueke has played a handful of games on the left since joining Arsenal from Chelsea but it hasn’t happened nearly as frequently as had been expected when he first arrived. A left-footer on the left wing: old-school!

Right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

#1409. A death sentence for ‘sloppy’ cancers

In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Lorenzo Valcanover is in the Division of Oncogenomics, Oncode Institute, the Netherlands Cancer Institute, Amsterdam 1066 CX, the Netherlands.

Reuven Agami is in the Division of Oncogenomics, Oncode Institute, the Netherlands Cancer Institute, Amsterdam 1066 CX, the Netherlands, and the Department of Genetics, Erasmus University Rotterdam, the Netherlands.

Identifying cellular properties that distinguish a cancer from healthy tissue is a crucial step for developing efficient treatments. One such characteristic is the ‘sloppy’ way in which some cancer cells implement translation — the process by which proteins are made from messenger RNA by protein complexes called ribosomes. This process can go awry. Writing in Nature, Wang et al.1 reveal a cancer-specific mechanism by which translation loses its normal ‘track’ of how it reads an mRNA sequence to encode the expected amino acids, resulting in a phenomenon called frameshifting. This generates proteins that have a distinct sequence of amino acids that are not usually made, and the authors show that this abnormality might be exploited for therapeutic purposes.

#1408. Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager said. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw

It had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick said: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”

When asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

3 - Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? https://t.co/DuSpvymZfu

The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

“We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

“We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”

"They look devoid of any confidence" Jamie Redknapp says Manchester United's squad is not strong enough ❌ https://t.co/oZgmtWelJB

More jeers at the final whistle from United fans - they weren’t happy with this point against a team there for the taking after Rodrigo Bentancur’s dismissal. Michael Carrick is still trying to find answers because this United team is not clicking.

The late chaos is over at Old Trafford as Solanke rescues a precious point for Tottenham with that 92nd minute equaliser. Man Utd thought they had the game wrapped up after Mbeumo’s well-taken opener was followed by Bentancur’s crazy red card. However, Spurs, who were the better team throughout the contest, kept fighting and found a fully deserved leveller. The visitors remain winless, but it’s another worrying performance from Carrick’s side, who have picked up just one victory in six top-flight matches.

A point apiece in Manchester. https://t.co/xiEiQsFsje

Dalot and Gray are both handed yellow cards for fouls that broke up play. Despite their numerical disadvantage, Spurs currently look like the more likely side to claim a victory.

It’s just the Spurs fans singing in Old Trafford now. They fully deserved that equaliser. Rashford and Heaven are on for the hosts, with Cunha and Shaw taken off.

Incredible drama at Old Trafford! Tonali floats a cross into the box and Solanke shrugs off Martinez, before flicking a delicate header into the bottom corner to send Spurs’ away support wild. Man Utd are stunned. Could the visitors go on and win this now?

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw

Van Hecke does well to block Cunha’s effort and the referee indicates that there will be a minimum of eight minutes of added time.

De Zerbi’s final roll of the dice in search of a late leveller sees Fernandes replace Senesi for the remaining few minutes. Spurs must throw everyone forward now.

Martinez lunges in on Maddison and brings down the playmaker with a foul. The centre-back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Baleba unleashes Mbeumo with an over-the-top through ball. Racing through on goal, the forward shoots, but from an unfavourable angle, Kinsky parries his near post effort out for a corner.

Fernandes is cautioned after catching Van Hecke with a late challenge on his ankle. Spurs players aren’t happy with the tackle.

Bentancur’s recklessness has left Spurs with a mountain to climb. Their chance of a comeback looks a bit slimmer now that Man Utd have a numerical advantage on the pitch.

It’s all kicked off at Old Trafford! Bentancur flies in with a risky challenge on Shaw. The Man Utd defender is furious with the tackle and the two players square up to each other. Shaw pushes Bentancur over and the midfielder responds by leaning into the Englishman, creating a headbutt-like action. Shaw and Van Hecke are also given yellows for their roles in that altercation.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc

Rodrigo Bentancur is sent off... and here's why ⬇️ https://t.co/3ahzz5iUbg

Spurs respond to going behind by making a double change as Van de Ven and Maddison come on to replace Udogie and Gallagher.

It’s against the run of play, but Man Utd won’t care, they have the all-important advantage! Cunha runs into a channel and slips a pass into Mbeumo. Van Hecke allows the forward to turn and Mbeumo slides a delightful effort into the far bottom corner. Old Trafford erupts in joy. Tottenham can’t believe it.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe

Tonali’s pass is intercepted by Maguire, but the ball trickles into the onrushing Savio’s path. The winger’s powerful first-time effort is blocked by Mainoo’s sliding challenge and flies over the bar.

It’s Tottenham’s turn to make some alterations as Bentancur and Marmoush enter the action, replacing Bergvall and Kudus.

Zirkzee turns Senesi and threads a pass through to Fernandes. From a tight angle, the Man Utd captain slices a ferocious effort into the side netting. The playmaker has been quiet today, but you can never write him off from scoring or providing an assist.

Baleba’s first action in a Man Utd shirt sees the midfielder smash a hopeful volley wildly off target. Can Baleba’s introductrion lift the crowd and help give the hosts some impetus?

Carrick has seen enough, ordering a much-needed triple change. Baleba replaces Tielemans to make his Man Utd debut. The other changes see Amad and Yoro withdrawn for Zirkzee and Dalot.

🔛 Here comes Carlos! 🇨🇲 Our no.20 makes his United debut as part of a triple change... https://t.co/jGEL8ui0PI

Van Hecke wins the header at the back post of a corner, looping the ball right back into the danger zone, but Maguire is there to crucially nod it over the bar.

Man Utd have the ball in the net, but it won’t count, as Cunha failed to keep it in play before teeing up Tielemans to finish from close range. Old Trafford thought it had lift-off against the run of play, but they’ve been denied by the correct decision.

Tottenham will be kicking themselves! Once again, Savio is causing trouble for Man Utd, driving at the home side’s defence before crossing for Solanke. The striker beats Martinez to the delivery, but directs his half-volley over the bar. That is another hugely frustrating passage of play for Spurs, and yet another missed opportunity. De Zerbi can’t believe it.

How have Tottenham not scored there?! Savio races through after latching onto Tonali’s piercing pass. Maguire can’t keep up with the winger’s pace as he reaches the byline. Kudus and Solanke are waiting for a tap-in inside the six-yard box, but the ball lands at Shaw’s feet, and he clears.

A promising spell of Man Utd pressure ends with Van Hecke stretching to clear Shaw’s searching delivery out for a corner.

We are back under way for the second half at Old Trafford. Both sides are unchanged at the break.

That’s the question De Zerbi will be asking himself and his players at half-time...

Boos greet the half-time whistle as Man Utd have underperformed on their return to Premier League action. However, luckily for the hosts, Tottenham have lacked composure in front of goal, with Solanke, Kudus and Gallagher all missing notable chances.

Nothing to separate @ManUtd and @SpursOfficial at half-time... https://t.co/yJc8pvyfLl

There will be one minute of added time to round off this first half.

Spurs go close again! Solanke plays in Gallagher, who bundles his way into the six-yard box. Tielemans, Martinez and Yoro all fail to apprehend the Spurs midfielder, who digs a close-range shot out of his feet. However, Lammens is there to make a crucial block and thwart the visitors.

Spurs have been on top in this half but there has been a lack of quality from both teams. It has been a scrap between two average teams. Conor Gallagher the most influential player on the pitch so far.

Following Solanke and Kudus’ earlier chances, Spurs have been quiet going forward. Man Utd have been slowly growing into the game.

Amad is dribbling with intent and Gallagher bumps into him. The referee doesn’t give a free-kick and the home fans aren’t happy with that decision. It’s also worth remembering that Gallagher is on a yellow card. He needs to be careful.

Amad forces a save from Kinsky! Man Utd clear a Tottenham corner and burst forward on the counter through Mbeumo. The former Brentford man is chased by Tonali and has Amad in support, before playing the pass into the 24-year-old. Udogie closes down the angle, forcing Amad to take the chance with a first-time shot. His fizzing strike is comfortably collected by Kinsky, but that is more encouraging from the hosts.

You can feel the nervousness in the Old Trafford crowd. Spurs’ dominance has calmed over the last 10 minutes, but Man Utd have failed to take control or pick up the tempo.

This game looks it could be time for Baleba’s much-anticipated debut. Man Utd’s current midfield doesn’t possess enough running power and Tottenham are exploiting that.

Man Utd’s slow start prompts some boos from the home fans. Cunha attempts to rally the crowd, but his side have given their supporters nothing to be positive about in this game so far. From a Spurs perspective, you can see why they’ve only scored two top-flights goals this season. They should be two-nil up, but they’ve notably lacked end-product.

Tottenham miss another golden chance! It’s a brilliant passing move from defence to attack. It ends with Savio teeing up Kudus with an intelligent cross. The Ghanaian can’t quite fully wrap his foot around the delivery, and from inside the penalty area, he slams an unmarked effort wide of the bottom corner.

Currently, Man Utd are being outnumbered in midfield. The interchangeability of Tonali, Bergvall and Gallagher is running rings around Mainoo and Tielemans. Fernandes’ lack of defensive instinct is leaving the hosts’ midfield pivot exposed.

Man Utd then make a rare foray forward as Cunha whips in a cross towards Amad. Udogie is alert to the danger and gets in front of the winger to clear.

Ex-Nottingham Forest manager Steve Cooper is here in the directors’ box at Old Trafford. He was last at Brondby in Denmark and will inevitably be considered for jobs here in England as chairmen look to make changes during the season.

Still, it’s Tottenham forcing the issue as Kudus dashes past Shaw with his blistering pace. Cunha tracks back but can’t stop the winger from digging out a cross. Yoro’s skewed clearance is headed back to Lammens by Tielemans. Man Utd need to careful, they cannot continue playing like this.

The visitors then steam forward again on the counter. On this occasion, Yoro defends magnificently, executing a well-timed sliding tackle on Van Hecke.

#1407. Some are calling this 'Tuchel 2.0' and his latest squad does feel like that. Here's why England think a tilt at the European Championship is within reach, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 17:35 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 05:45 EST, 9 November 2026

One of Thomas Tuchel’s favourite analogies when it comes to the development of his England team is that of a train leaving a station with only the chosen few on it. As time moves on, the bodies lying on the tracks are growing greater in number.

Consider this statistic. Of the 26 players who travelled to the World Cup in America 13 are not in the squad chosen by England manager Tuchel for next week’s Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. And that does not include Cole Palmer and Phil Foden who, after missing out in the summer, were expected by many of us to have forced a way back in by now.

Tuchel’s latest selection has been affected by injuries, of course. But more significant is that the experienced German believes he is now starting to see an England team and squad develop in a way and in a direction that even he hadn’t envisaged once Argentina ended his World Cup hopes in that dismal Atlanta semi-final in July.

Different feelings, different style of play and, to a degree, different players.

Some are calling this ‘Tuchel 2.0’ and it does feel a little bit like that. The start of the second phase of Tuchel’s tenure, the start of the road towards a tilt at another trophy, the European Championships of 2028.

Having admitted to some worry ahead of the four-game international break FIFA saddled us all with last month, Tuchel sat down yesterday looking and sounding like a man once again certain of himself.

Tuchel sat down with the media looking and sounding like a man once again certain of himself

The inclusion of Jobe Bellingham — Jude’s younger brother (right) — was the headline act but there were other messages written within

Certain enough of a direct, quick, athletic style of play that helped England to two wins over Czech Republic and one – by seven goals – against Croatia in Rijeka. And certain that a dependence on players like Jordan Henderson, Dan Burn and John Stones for what we may politely call ‘squad culture management’ lies now in the past.

All of this may crash down in Madrid next Sunday. Spain have already beaten Tuchel’s England once – at Wembley in late September – and a repeat this month would ask familiar questions about England against the really good teams.

But for now, Tuchel is confident enough to claim that he has found his path.

‘We said at some point we need to take the next step, to build on what we have, to get better and to improve otherwise you’re just left behind,’ said Tuchel yesterday.

‘That’s how football works. You have been champion in one season but you need to improve, you need to bring in new players for competition, young players, new energy, fresh energy. It’s also the way, naturally, the national team goes.

‘We cannot be stuck in the same personnel and in the same style of play.

‘I agreed with you last month. I was the first to admit I was not 100 per cent happy with the pure level of football we played in the US. I saw a higher level in training [than on the field], I saw a higher level in glimpses.

‘We adjusted some things tactically, created some new positions and took the next steps.’

The Tuchel we sat down with in late September still wore the scars of the summer’s disappointment – and the criticism that came with it – rather visibly. It was the first time we had seen him like that in his two years in the job. He was tetchy and easily provoked. Call it the Argentina effect if you like.

Here, he appeared rather healed. Good results tend to do that for a manager and a little time helps too. If he believes his team has moved on then maybe he has also and he had to.

Certainly, his selection squad speaks to that. The inclusion of Jobe Bellingham – Jude’s younger brother – was the headline act but there were other messages written within.

Henderson and Burn are available but not included. So too Arsenal’s Noni Madueke, excluded to the benefit of the more direct Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha.

‘We need runners who will go between the lines,’ said Tuchel. A clear indication, there, that too much of England’s summer wing play was too slow and too conservatively narrow.

Palmer, Foden and Kobbie Mainoo are also on the outside looking in once again and the case of the Manchester United midfielder is perhaps indicative of how Tuchel now operates.

Moved to apologise to him in front of the whole squad in July for his lack of minutes at the World Cup, Tuchel was determined Mainoo would play in the opening four games of the Nations League campaign.

‘I was desperate to give him the minutes and desperate to include him in this new start,’ explained Tuchel.

‘But then he pulled out. He missed an excellent camp and also entered a difficult, difficult spell for himself.

‘Man United fell off a cliff a little bit performance-wise. So this is why he now suffers.’

We can talk about the whys and wherefores of that logic. If Mainoo was good enough in September then why is he not good enough now? How desperate could Tuchel really have been to play him that one withdrawal with injury closed the door for the next camp and opened it instead for Bellingham jnr?

This, though, is how Tuchel works. He is an adept tactician but he’s also a mood coach, someone who – after sobering club experiences at places like PSG, Chelsea and Bayern Munich – places huge emphasis on environments and gut feels and culture. If he feels something works, he doesn’t like to pick it apart without good reason.

This is why for example the growing voice and influence of Elliot Anderson has left Jordan Henderson suddenly surplus. Tuchel says the door is not closed on a player who will be 38 by the time the next Euros are played and he called him this week to say so. In Tuchel’s mind, though, England will now move without the veteran and others of his ilk.

‘I was concerned before the last camp that we missed the players who kept our standards,’ said Tuchel.

‘I was worried that we missed so many of them. But then this group found their own way and their own voices.

It’s also reasonable to ask why our head coach can’t find room in his squad – if not his team – for the game changing duo of Palmer and Foden

‘I know what the others did. They built a platform on which these ones can build.’

Time will tell. To a degree, Spain will tell. Can England play the kind of higher tempo, front foot football we saw against Croatia and the Czechs against the world and European champions next Sunday? They embarrassed us when we didn’t have the ball at Wembley.

It’s also reasonable to ask why our head coach can’t find room in his squad – if not his team – for the game-changing duo of Palmer and Foden. England lacked good substitutes at the World Cup. There was too much like for like.

England need to win in order for such decisions to be vindicated and Tuchel knows that.

Asked yesterday if he felt as invigorated as he looked he said he did. ‘The last camp gave me a lot of energy, gave me a lot of extra belief,’ he said.

‘It gave me a lot of optimism to not compromise on the way England teams should play. Be physical but also step up in the pure level of performances.’

It’s certainly time for this now. The summer only served to expose English shortcomings. Tuchel’s train must arrive in Madrid next weekend, not only with fresh personnel but also new ideas clearly apparent.

#1406. The cheats prosper: Man City thrash 10-man Liverpool

Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

This is a team who can stir the blood, surf the emotion and triumph against the odds more than any other; who have a proud history of doing so. Who feel the injustice at its most acute and could feed off that.

In the end Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the season. Their first under Andoni Iraola. And comprehensively so. It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

There was another sense of injustice. Up until the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, Liverpool were the better side. Especially as they attacked the Kop in the second half, drawing saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma, and began to build the kind of momentum that has, over the years, appeared to suck the ball into the net.

Ryan Gravenberch is OFF 🟥 https://t.co/IVIHNzqw6k

The midfielder’s first yellow card looked harsh. His second, for a foul on substitute Jérémy Doku was less so (but still not clear-cut) and it meant Liverpool had to play the final third of the game with 10 men. Instead of weaponising that; they wilted and the fans directed their frustration at referee Chris Kavanagh, believing he was lenient towards City.

This is not a slight on Iraola, but it is hard to imagine Jürgen Klopp not riding that wave of emotion more effectively and wringing more out of the available players. Turning to the fans; imploring them; cajoling them.

Instead it was City making the statement with an extraordinary power play as they scored three times in 13 minutes, inspired by Doku, whose cameo made him man of the match. That City could hold the winger back, on the bench, only to introduce him with such devastating effect again pointed to their phenomenal strength in depth.

They are again three points clear at the top, with six wins from six games, ahead of champions Arsenal and there is a frightening awesomeness about them at present that will make the Premier League shudder. For several reasons. What if they run away with it this season before being sanctioned, probably sometime in the spring? Where will that leave the competition?

In the face of City’s power and the adversity of losing Gravenberch, Liverpool simply could not cope. They were already depleted – without Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Cody Gakpo – and needed some of their other big signings to respond.

But this was not a good day for Bradley Barcola or Florian Wirtz, in particular, and it felt telling that the latter was withdrawn soon after Erling Haaland opened the scoring. He could, in fact, have also been sent off after catching Elliot Anderson late. The German’s contribution was once more woefully negligible; worryingly marginal. He was lightweight and so, ultimately, were Liverpool.

It captured City’s swagger, their sense of responding to what they regard as an injustice – that they maintain will be overturned on appeal – the sense they are going to continue to create an almighty headache for the Premier League. In a sea of uncertainty as to what will now happen, that is something we can be sure of.

“Cheats,” loudly boomed around Anfield from the home fans before the PA played Fleetwood Mac’s Tell Me Lies at the final whistle, as the players walked off. Enzo Maresca hailed Manchester City’s ability to “make our own noise” after their emphatic 3-0 win at Liverpool.

In the first fixture since being found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges laid against them for serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, City made their statement on the pitch as they re-established a three-point lead at the top of the table.

“It was not easy for the players after the last two, three weeks, but they dealt with it very well,” Maresca, the head coach, said. “I said during the week we need to learn to deal with the outside noise because of the situation, because that will be there. But we have to make our own noise.

“Zero-three at Anfield away is a great result, for sure. I think all the organisation needs a win like this. It’s good for all [of] the club.”

Maresca said City will have to get used to such hostile occasions, with Liverpool fans making clear their anger over the judgment, and added: “All the away games are going to be with noise.”

Maresca confirmed that chief executive Ferran Soriano and director of football Hugo Viana had travelled on the team bus to Anfield in a sign of unity.

“Ferran was there, Hugo was there. We were all together,” Maresca said. “For the importance of the game, Liverpool away, Anfield away. It’s good to be together.”

The Italian claimed that despite the verdict, and the attention and uncertainty as to what will happen next, it had not affected his squad.

“The players just focus on the football. They are not thinking about the future,” he said. “It’s how we learn to deal with the noise. It’s our duty to make noise and to do that we win games. You cannot imagine how happy I am. Hopefully I am going to speak about this situation when we are going to win the appeal.”

The Liverpool boss told BBC MOTD: “I think the first part is that we played two different games. One until the red card, and then after. For 60 minutes, the players were very good. The second game from the red card was where City were better than us.

“The first yellow card was just a kick in the toe. It was nothing. It was a normal foul. It was the moment when we were pushing more. The momentum was coming for us and the atmosphere in the stadium was so nice. We conceded very little in the first half. We did a really good job. The second half, we were translating into chances.

“You learn a lot in games like today. I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It’s a loss and we didn’t get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot.”

The hosts fly up the other end, with the busy Munoz running at O’Reilly. The City left-back has to match him stride for stride before conceding a corner.

Gravenberch tries to find Munoz with a threaded pass through City’s backline. However, O’Reilly defends expertly, shielding the ball back to his goalkeeper.

Liverpool need more from Wirtz and Barcola. Both big-money attackers have been on the periphery. With Isak, Gakpo and Szoboszlai all absent, Iraola needs the duo on the pitch to deliver.

Liverpool have been aggressive and on the front foot, but we’re still waiting for a noteworthy chance to be created here at Anfield. City haven’t been spectacular, but they’ve done just about enough so far.

Kerkez fires in a cross and there’s a miscommunication between Guehi and Donnarumma, with the centre-back slicing a clearance instead of allowing the goalkeeper to gather the delivery. Barcola can’t capitalise on the loose ball and City get away with one there.

Let’s not kid ourselves about what we are seeing at the moment. There is a lot of noise but nothing has happened to light a fire and the onus has got to be on Liverpool’s players to step this up considerably. This occasion, more than anything, is crying out for someone to play how the supporters are feeling and it’s not there yet. It’s been tame and Manchester City are, accordingly, comfortable.

City motor forward on the counter through Cherki, whose delightful touch takes him away from Mac Allister. From inside his own half, the Frenchman dribbles to the edge of Liverpool’s penalty area. He attempts to play a one-two with Fernandez, but the pass is cut out by Jacquet.

Manchester City have not got going, as of yet. The defiant message from the club is they would not let the verdict affect them. They have defended well enough but have barely strung a passing sequence together against a Liverpool side who appear be playing off pure emotion.

Gravenberch is bossing this game in midfield. Another powerful run from deep results in a delightful nutmeg on Fernandez, who slips over. Liverpool’s energy has been really impressive. City need to ride out this early storm.

It’s getting heated at Anfield! Mac Allister and Anderson clash sparking a scuffle between both sets of players. It threatened to boil over for a second, but the drama quickly calms down and play resumes after the referee has a word with the two captains.

All fairly difficult to stomach, the Manchester City fans’ performance at kick-off. Inflatable bananas to signify nostalgia for the late 1980s, when these were all the rage after the club’s relegation to Division Two? The City of Sheikh Mansour are about as far removed from the era of Jimmy Frizzell as is possible to imagine, with their colossal wealth enabling cheating on an unprecedented scale. And as for the Poznan during You’ll Never Walk Alone? When Liam Gallagher asks Oasis fans to perform this backwards dance during next year’s tour, I suspect there will not be quite the same take-up.

Amid all the build-up and backstory to this extraordinary fixture it is remarkable that 21-year-old Lewis Koumas is making his first Premier League start as Liverpool’s makeshift centre-forward. And he has started well.

A spell of Man City possession has slightly quelled the atmosphere. On paper, you would have to say the away side’s starting 11 is superior to Liverpool’s.

Liverpool make a fast start as Gravenberch effortlessly turns Fernandez and Munoz darts inside of O’Reilly. The winger’s shot is smothered by Guehi, but the early signs are encouraging for the hosts.

City get us under way at Anfield. This is one we’ve quite literally all been waiting for.

Since City last kicked a football in anger, they have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges levelled at them by the Premier League in a verdict that has shaken professional football to its very core. The club have appealed and the extent of their punishment now rests with an independent panel. City have put up a united front and on Thursday Maresca and Haaland duly delivered the party lines, the City head coach revealing that the feeling among his charges was “fantastic”. “[My players] know what we can control is the football side – they are not worried at all about different things,” Maresca said, before adding that he trusts the club “completely”. City are top of the league having won all five of their league matches so far, while Liverpool have huffed and puffed to sixth, remaining unbeaten.

#1405. Crisis-hit FIFA chief Gianni Infantino 'requested VIP treatment for his daughters and their dogs at Miami airport'

By DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 09:47 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 12:07 EST, 9 November 2026

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is facing more uncomfortable questions after it emerged that his office asked for 'VIP treatment' for his daughters and their pet dogs on a trip from Miami to Qatar.

Infantino's future has been under the microscope after a scandal-laden few months, with honorary Japanese FA president Kohzo Tashima announcing on Thursday that he will stand against Infantino in next year's presidential election.

On Thursday, The Times revealed that back in May, Infantino's presidential office wrote to Miami airport officials asking for someone to 'assist' three of his daughters - and their pets - through security for a personal trip to Qatar.

Miami airport's VIP protocol reportedly allows diplomats and other special guests to be escorted through security checkpoints up to the door of the plane. Officers can also request early boarding.

These privileges are not automatically laid on for loved ones traveling separately, with protocol stating that 'courtesies... will not be extended' to family members of VIPs 'when the families are traveling on their own.'

But according to documents reviewed by the Daily Mail, members of Infantino's family enjoyed the airport's services dozens of times while traveling without the FIFA president between 2024 and 2026.

Gianni Infantino's office reportedly requested 'VIP treatment' for his daughters and their dogs

The FIFA president's future has been under the microscope after a scandal-laden few months

In a statement to The Times, Miami airport insisted these requests are dealt with 'on a case-by-case basis.' The Daily Mail has contacted FIFA for comment but a spokesperson told The Times: 'Port courtesy requests were made to Miami international airport (MIA), on the advice of a former adviser to the Fifa president.

'Port courtesies are provided at no charge to the president of Fifa given his position as the head of an association or NGO. Mr Infantino’s family members are also entitled to request these services under MIA’s own Courtesies of Port Handbook and these are also provided free of any charge, on a case-by-case basis, at the discretion of MIA.'

Infantino's position is already under threat heading into FIFA's presidential election next March, when he is hoping to be elected to a fourth term. Back in December, Infantino awarded Trump the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize – to widespread ridicule.

During the World Cup, the Balogun affair saw Infantino accused of favoritism and caving to the White House, while the FIFA president and Trump were mocked for handing over the trophy to Spain together.

Before long, Infantino faced a mutiny over his secret plans – later scrapped – to sell a stake in the World Cup to private equity investors including Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.

Then earlier this week, FIFA strongly denied allegations that Infantino influenced Trump administration officials to fast-track a work permit for his undocumented Nicaraguan housekeeper after she lost her legal status, according to bombshell documents.

The global soccer chief is alleged to have turned to politically-connected contacts to secure a new work permit for Yajarlin del Socorro Fernandez after the White House revoked her legal permission to work in the United States, according to documents reviewed by the Daily Mail.

#1404. Epileptic seizures nearly vanish after people receive experimental gene therapy in their brains

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Mariana Lenharo is a reporter for Nature in New York City.

A scan shows the brain of a man with epilepsy. A newly developed gene therapy targets locations in the brain that are the root of epileptic seizures. Credit: Allison Robbert/The Washington Post/Getty

Three people with epilepsy resistant to drug treatment saw the number of seizures they had per month fall by more than 90% after gene-laden viruses were infused directly into their brains as part of an early-stage clinical trial1.

In each participant, the gene therapy was precisely targeted to a small patch of brain tissue that was the source of their seizures. The viruses carried a gene that makes neurons sensitive to a specific drug, which works like a dimmer switch for the therapy. By combining gene therapy with a drug — an approach known as chemogenetics — researchers can adjust a treatment’s potency, which is not possible with other types of gene therapy. The trial participants did not experience serious side effects.

Genetic therapies offer new hope against incurable brain diseases

Genetic therapies offer new hope against incurable brain diseases

The results were reported today in The New England Journal of Medicine by Yang Dai, a neurosurgeon at Xuanwu Hospital of Capital Medical University in Beijing, and his colleagues. “It’s exciting that there’s such a dramatic effect, and that they see very few side effects,” says Matthew Walker, a neurologist at University College London, who was not associated with the study.

But Walker cautions that the study is small. He is also concerned about the long-term use of the drug that participants took after receiving the gene therapy. High doses of the drug, an anti-psychotic called clozapine, have been associated with cardiovascular problems and other negative effects. “In the future, hopefully there are going to be better drugs” for this form of treatment, says Walker, who is the co-founder of the start-up company Focalis Bio in Canterbury, UK, which is also developing gene therapies for epilepsy.

The three trial participants were adults with a common form of epilepsy caused by hippocampal sclerosis, a type of scarring in a region of the brain called the hippocampus. The participants had this scarring on only one side of the hippocampus. All three had been diagnosed with epilepsy 10–25 years earlier and had developed resistance to at least two anti-seizure drugs. They also had at least two seizure episodes per month, on average, over the three months before they enrolled in the trial.

The experimental treatment uses a virus called adeno-associated virus 9 to deliver a gene to neurons in the affected area. The gene was engineered to produce proteins specifically in excitatory cells — the ones that are involved in seizures.

Brain editing now ‘closer to reality’: the gene-altering tools tackling deadly disorders

Brain editing now ‘closer to reality’: the gene-altering tools tackling deadly disorders

The gene instructs neurons to produce a receptor that binds to clozapine. Clozapine acts like a switch and activates these receptors, reducing the activity of the targeted neurons, the authors say. That reduced activity helps to suppress the abnormal electrical activity that triggers seizures.

Two weeks after receiving the gene therapy during surgery, participants began taking a low dose of clozapine every eight hours. Around two months later, the average number of seizures per month had dropped from 4.5 to 0.5 for two of the participants and from 4 to 0 for the third. Because the study design focused on safety, rather than measuring efficacy, there was no control group.

Walker says that there might be other explanations for the improvement. He adds that it is also not clear whether the effect was because of the combination of gene therapy and clozapine or from one of those components alone.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03566-2

#1403. Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”

Matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

“It was an outstanding performance,” the manager said. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the new arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

Even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a new look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

That may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

The 4-1 thrashing at Leeds in their last away game was a painful reminder of the team’s vulnerability. They were bullied and outclassed.

Newcastle have not put together an impressive 90-minute performance since the opening day draw with Liverpool, yet that defeat to Leeds was also the only game they have lost. in all competitions. We will know a lot more about them after this. This is a game they are expected to win, so the ramifications of a defeat will be more severe.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline says. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

#1402. Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”

Avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

England thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

“Not really [a moment she had dreamt about] to be honest because I’m a defender and I thought I’d just be stopping it but it’s always good to get up there. When I play that position, I find myself a little bit higher up, definitely something to work on but very happy to score my first goal.

“I do [like playing that position], I love defending as well. It’s obviously a bit different for me up there but I always try and give my best whatever position I play so I did enjoy it.”

Tonight’s hosts are yet to qualify for a major tournament and are expected to set up in a defensive shape. England defender Esme Morgan believes the squad are ready for a long night of breaking down a stubborn opposition.

She told a pre-match press conference: “It’s just about persistence and trying not to get drawn into being frustrated by the opposition. A really good example was the away game against Ukraine in qualifying. We couldn’t seem to break through in the first half - the keeper was making saves, we hit the woodwork - but the messaging at half-time was just to keep continuing because we were creating opportunities.

”Not to start snatching or taking shots from distance, just trusting in our style of play and our ability to find gaps. We came out for the second half and scored really quickly. It’s just about sticking to the plan and being patient.”

Erica Meg Parkinson, one of England’s new midfielders, was apparently named after Eric Cantona.

While Cantona still famously is proud of his kung fu kick, when he attacked an obnoxious Crystal Palace fan, Parkison is less enthused by football’s most famous case of breaking the fourth wall.

“My dad is a huge Man United fan so I was named after Eric Cantona,” Parkinson says. “It’s a pretty good player to be named after except for, you know, the karate kicks.

“My brother was named after Denis Law. I don’t think my mum had much of a say in the name so she was dragged into it, but it kind of worked out because we both play football now.”

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

“Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman said. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

“That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”

Toone quickly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven big-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

#1401. Arsenal’s big guns blow Lille away after the second string flop

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

The three big guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

That was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the big three were on the difference was obvious.

The Arsenal players wore black armbands to mark the passing, aged 94, of Ken Friar, the club’s life vice-president. He had served the club from 1945 to 2014 and was variously club secretary, managing director and a driving force in building the stadium in which they now play. Even Arteta, no sentimentalist, insisted on beginning his press conference with a tribute.

For Arteta’s players, there will be a much bigger test than this one in Munich next week against Bayern. Arsenal have already won in Naples but a victory at Bayern would be significant beyond that. Arsenal have won all but one of their 10 games this season – that big defeat at the Amex Stadium, almost one month ago. They clearly have another gear to go to when required although ideally, Arteta would not always have to ask it of the same players. The club have spent too much on this squad not to be able to trust the understudies.

Madueke did at least end the game with an assist. Of Saka’s understudy, Arteta said: “When you talk about players being clinical – what is clinical? Clinical sometimes means that they score one in every 500. It’s about generating volume and more actions and getting him into the good position because he will decide matches.”

No goals for Gyokeres this season and a general acceptance that the time for persevering with him has passed. It could be ever-dwindling returns for him in terms of game-time as the season goes. Coming off the bench for Lille in the second half was the unmistakable Olivier Giroud, now 40 and more than 14 years on since he signed for Arsenal from Montpellier. He was given a warm welcome by the home fans and, later, an equally warm farewell despite the Chelsea years in the interim. He was a much better player than Gyokeres in an era when Arsenal were in decline.

Michael Olise was sent off in Bayern Munich’s draw at Viking, meaning he will miss next week’s game against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena.

Since returning to the competition under Arteta in 2023, they have won all 12 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals.

Including knock-out games, Arsenal have conceded just eight goals in 20 home matches, keeping 15 clean sheets.

Four of those goals came in effective dead rubbers against PSV in the 2025 last-16 (after Arsenal won 7-1 in Eindhoven) and against Kairat Almaty in the final game of last season’s league phase.

So in home Champions League games that matter, they have conceded just four goals in 18 matches: Serge Gnarby and Harry Kane for Bayern in the 2024 quarter-final, Ousmane Dembele in the 2025 semi-final and Lennart Karl for Bayern in last season’s league phase.

Lille are considering legal ⁠action after defender Tiago Santos suffered a serious knee injury following an “uncontrolled and dangerous” tackle in Saturday’s match ‌against Le Havre.

Santos, 24, suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tear in his right knee and was carried off the pitch on a stretcher after being tackled by Le Havre midfielder Amir Richardson during the first half of Lille’s 1-0 victory.

The referee gave a foul for the tackle but did not issue Richardson with a caution.

Lille said the ‌tackle merited ‌a red card ⁠and that they had asked the league’s governing body (LFP) to refer the matter to its disciplinary committee. The club are also seeking an explanation of ⁠the video review process undertaken by match officials.

Will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium?
